content.text:
I submitted **index 5 (Sb fraction 0.231)** as the best composition. At 0.0735% it had the highest EQE of the five I measured. The whole EQE budget is used; I used 3 of the 5 XRD measurements.

| Index | Sb fraction | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0.142 | 0.0449 |
| **5** | **0.231** | **0.0735** |
| 7 | 0.271 | 0.0584 |
| 14 | 0.488 | 0.0156 |
| 22 | 0.712 | 0.0046 |

- **Where the peak is:** EQE is best at low Sb and falls steeply above about 0.3 Sb. The Sb-rich end of the line is poor.
- **Structure:** XRD at Sb 0.14, 0.23 and 0.31 gave the same single-phase pattern. So EQE seems to change with composition within one crystal phase, not because the phase changes. I think it may be the rutile-type FeSbO₄ structure, but I didn't check it against simulated patterns.
- **Last measurement:** a curve fitted to my first three EQE points put the peak near Sb 0.29, so I spent the final measurement on index 7 (0.271). It came in lower than index 5, which suggests the true peak is around 0.23.

The best composition could still be unmeasured. Indices 3, 4 and 6 (Sb 0.19–0.25) sit right next to index 5 and could come in slightly higher.
